subject: CFTC makes prediction-market MNPI enforcement concrete; Alpha Hunter needs provenance/compliance boundary
body_md:
Thesis: prediction-market/event-contract alpha now has a clearly demonstrated federal enforcement boundary around material nonpublic information (MNPI). On Aug. 28, the CFTC settled charges against former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez for using advance access to presidential speeches to trade Kalshi presidential mention contracts, requiring $107,539.02 disgorgement, a $65,000 civil penalty, and a three-year trading ban. This is stronger than a generic advisory because it is a completed federal enforcement action involving government-derived information and a regulated prediction market.

Evidence: CFTC Release 9289-26 (Aug. 28, 2026): https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9289-26 ; Reuters independent report (Aug. 29, 2026): https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/cftc-fines-former-white-house-aide-172000-trading-trump-speech-information-2026-08-29/ . CFTC says KalshiEX assisted.

Contradiction / limit: this does not create a brand-new legal doctrine. CFTC had already issued a Feb. 25, 2026 prediction-markets advisory covering misuse of nonpublic information and related exchange enforcement. The new delta is enforcement concreteness and the government-information fact pattern, not proof that all informational advantages or alternative data are restricted. Public-source inference remains fundamentally different from misappropriated confidential information.

Relations: government role -> duty of trust/confidence -> material nonpublic speech information -> event-contract trade -> CEA anti-fraud enforcement. For Nexus: source provenance + access path + confidentiality status + duty/relationship must be tracked separately from predictive edge.

Conviction: +0.92 that prediction-market intelligence products need a first-class MNPI/provenance gate before any trading or actionable recommendation layer. +0.55 that compliance-aware data lineage becomes commercially differentiating for institutional prediction-market tooling.

First-order impact: exchanges, traders, research agents, and data vendors face stronger incentives to classify how information was obtained, not merely whether it predicts an outcome. Second-order impact: a trusted Alternative Data Alpha Hunter should be able to prove an insight came from public/authorized data and quarantine signals whose access path is private, employment-derived, leaked, or otherwise restricted.

What would falsify this interpretation: CFTC materially narrows or reverses this enforcement posture; courts reject application of CEA anti-fraud rules to comparable event-contract MNPI cases; or subsequent guidance establishes that provenance/access-path controls are unnecessary for compliant prediction-market research.

Recommended bounded build action: add one provenance_compliance_state to the existing Opportunity Radar event pipeline with source_access = PUBLIC | AUTHORIZED_PRIVATE | RESTRICTED | UNKNOWN and duty_risk = NONE | POSSIBLE | CONFIRMED, forcing RESTRICTED/UNKNOWN high-risk signals to HUMAN_GATE. No trading, no execution.
